summary: Defines a method for an edge router in an Ethernet-based aggregation network to identify the subscriber premises that sent a Router Solicitation message. Several premises may share one router interface, and the option uses content of the received message. It is limited to broadband access. It is a standards-track specification.

eli5.summary: Many houses share one entrance. This memo adds a tag so the router can tell which house sent a given message.

questions: how to identify subscriber lines in ipv6 router solicitation
what is the ipv6 line-identification option
how does an access node tunnel router solicitations
subtitle: How an access node tags IPv6 Router Solicitations so the edge router knows which subscriber line they came from.

tldr.problem: When many subscriber lines share one VLAN to an Edge Router (the N:1 VLAN model), the router cannot tell which line a Router Solicitation came from.
tldr.mechanism: The Access Node tunnels each Router Solicitation inside an IPv6 packet carrying a Line-Identification destination option (type 0x8C) with a Line ID, and the Edge Router tunnels the Router Advertisement back with the same option.
tldr.outcome: The router can pick the right prefix and policy per line, but the design is limited to N:1 VLAN broadband deployments and has no way to detect an inactive subscriber.

today: RFC 6788 is a Proposed Standard and the metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: The Broadband Access Problem
sections.content:
Some DSL and GPON networks are moving from PPP to an IP-based Ethernet aggregation network. In the N:1 VLAN model, user ports behind one or more Access Nodes (AN, also called a DSLAM) map to the same VLAN toward the Edge Router, also known as the Broadband Network Gateway (BNG).

An end-device normally sends a Router Solicitation (RS) and gets a Router Advertisement (RA) with a prefix for address autoconfiguration. But in an N:1 VLAN the Edge Router has no way to tell which circuit the RS arrived on. With DHCP, a relay agent adds that information. RFC 6788 provides an equivalent for hosts that use only IPv6 stateless address autoconfiguration.
sections.eli5: Lots of homes send questions through one shared pipe. The router needs to know which home asked, so it can give the right answer.

sections.title: Where It Applies
sections.content:
The Line-Identification Option (LIO) is intended only for the N:1 VLAN model. The AN also starts RSes of its own, which makes the system more robust than relying on the end-device's few initial retransmissions. The cost is that, since no frame arrives from the subscriber for an AN-sent RS, the Edge Router cannot learn the subscriber's MAC address.

  • NOT RECOMMENDED where the endpoint MAC address is needed for identification.
  • NOT RECOMMENDED where automatic notice that a subscriber is no longer active is needed.
  • The mechanism does not by itself protect against loss of RS-induced state in access routers, so it SHOULD only be used with N:1 VLANs.
sections.eli5: This trick only works for one kind of network, and it cannot tell when a home has moved out.

sections.title: Tunneling the Messages
sections.content:
The AN intercepts an ICMPv6 type 133 Router Solicitation and tunnels it, as in RFC 2473, inside a new IPv6 datagram with a destination options header holding the LIO. The inner Hop Limit MUST NOT be decremented, because a Neighbor Discovery message whose Hop Limit is not 255 is discarded by its receiver.

The outer source address is the AN's own address if it has one, otherwise the source of the RS. The outer destination is copied from the RS. The Line ID identifies the logical access loop port the RS came from.

The Edge Router looks up addressing information and policy from the Line ID, then processes the inner RS as in RFC 4861. Its RA MUST include a Prefix Information option for the prefix that matches the LIO, and it is tunneled back with the same Line ID. The AN removes the outer header and multicasts the original RA on that subscriber circuit only.
sections.eli5: The access node puts each question in an envelope marked with the home's label. The router answers in an envelope with the same label, and the access node delivers it to just that home.

sections.title: Access Node and Edge Router Duties
sections.content:
On start-up the AN MUST join the All-BBF-Access-Nodes multicast group (ff02::10) on its upstream interfaces. When a subscriber circuit comes up, the AN MUST create its own RS from the unspecified source address and tunnel it, so that the Edge Router starts sending periodic RAs. The AN SHOULD keep retransmitting with exponential backoff until it gets an RA for that LIO, with an initial retransmission time of 1 second and a maximum of 30 seconds. If it detects Edge Router failure, it repeats this for each live circuit.

If the received outer source was not the unspecified address, the Edge Router copies it into the outer destination. If it was unspecified, the outer destination is ff02::10. The router MUST NOT send tunneled RAs larger than the link MTU, because the AN may not handle reassembly.

After the first RA, the Edge Router MUST store the LIO-to-prefix mapping and send periodic unsolicited RAs, tunneled the same way. It MAY stop if the AN reports the circuit down, for example through ANCP.
sections.eli5: The access node keeps knocking until the router answers, and the router keeps sending friendly reminders afterward to every home it knows about.

sections.title: The Line-Identification Option
sections.content:
The LIO is an IPv6 destination option. Its fields are the Option Type (0x8C), an 8-bit Option Length that MUST be greater than 0, an 8-bit LineIDLen and a variable-length Line ID. It has no alignment requirement, and a datagram MUST NOT contain more than one.

The Line ID MUST be unique across all ANs sharing a link to the Edge Router. It uses only US-ASCII characters from decimal 32 to 126, mirroring the DHCP relay options, and the high-order bit of each octet MUST be zero. It SHOULD NOT contain NUL, but receivers MUST NOT fail if one is present. Comparison is byte by byte, so f123 is not equal to F123, and intermediate systems MUST NOT alter it.
sections.eli5: The label is a short piece of plain text. Two labels match only if every letter is exactly the same, even capital letters.

sections.title: Security and Housekeeping
sections.content:
The line identification inserted by the AN or Edge Router is not protected, so it can be modified, inserted or deleted undetected. The network between the AN and the Edge Router needs to be trusted for the Line ID to be believed.

Because the RS and RA inside the tunnel are not changed, SEcure Neighbor Discovery verification is unaffected. A prefix stays tied to a line even while the line is down, and can be reclaimed only by manual action that dissociates it from the LIO in the backend systems.
sections.eli5: The labels are not locked, so the road between the access node and the router has to be trusted. Giving a label back takes a person doing it by hand.

fields.name: Option Length
fields.desc: Length of the option excluding Option Type and Option Length; greater than 0.

fields.name: LineIDLen
fields.desc: Length of the Line ID field in octets.
